title: Grandfather's Oklahoma homesteading story and its lesson
summary: His grandfather, a former slave, sold his Texas land to homestead in Oklahoma but was too religious to claim it; Thomas says this taught him to get an education.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I guess it's a good time to talk about my grandfather.

My grandfather... See, Oklahoma opened the territory, and I don't know what year it was; it must have been eighteen-something. And he sold... I understand that my Grandfather was a slave. So his slave-owner gave him and

all his dependents, his children, some of the best black-bottom land in Texas. He sold everybody's land, sold his, my mother's and everybody else's, to get money to go to Oklahoma. So the deal was, they drove up to the Oklahoma-Texas border, and they had to stay on the Texas side until twelve o'clock at night.
What was the reason for that?

Well, they had to wait until twelve o'clock, because that was the time to go in, twelve o'clock at night. I don't know the reason. But twelve o'clock at night is when they'd sound the trumpet or shoot the gun or something, and then everybody would go over and homestead.
Oh yeah. I remember hearing about that.

And I ran into some of my relatives down in Texas, Luther Manning, and he told me the story about my grandfather. He said when they...whatever signal they gave to go in... He said my grandmother was sitting on the horse asleep! And boy, the Manning family was a sleeping family. We could sleep anywhere...
And that was your mother's side?
That was my mother's side. And so he said he was sleeping. And my grandfather was a vagabond. He

traveled.... He didn't stay no place no length of time. My grandmother told me this story. One thing about him, he was too religious to take some of that land. They was givin' the land away! Wasn't no (?). They wanted you to come in there and homestead it and use it. It was yours. And he'd have got enough land for his dependents if he'd known. But my grandmother said he was too religious. He thought he was taking something from somebody. And here they was, givin' it away.

And Milt, that one little incident had a lot to do with my life. Because I saw how the different natives had land, and then they didn't have it, and half of them didn't get an education. And that influenced on me to go and learn something so... I didn't have no land. And I guess I can start... The earliest I know is in kindergarten.
